messages.subject: Soft links in windows
parts:
Hi,

I tried to use soft links for mapping a directory holding CEL files in
the default directory structure like that:

<working_dir>/rawData/<my_project>/<chiptype>

where <chiptype> is a link to the folder holding the CEL files. The
folder I link to is called e.g. <somepath>/"DLBCLwMLBCL.chipA".

I can't get aroma.affymetrix to accept this link. I use
AffymetrixCelSet$byName() or AffymetrixCelSet$fromFile(), but aroma
complains like this.

> ds <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("rawData/Monti/HG-U133A")
Error en list(`AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("rawData/Monti/HG-U133A")` =
<environment>, :

[2009-08-07 12:43:48] Exception: Invalid name of directory containing
CEL files. The name of the directory (DLBCLwMLBCL.chipA) must be the
same as the chip type used for the CEL files (HG-U133A) unless using
argument 'checkChipType=FALSE': D:/hilmar/DataSets/Monti/
DLBCLwMLBCL.chipA
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Invalid name of directory containing CEL files.
The name of the directory (", chipType, ") must be the same as the
chip type used for t
at throw("Invalid name of directory containing CEL files. The name
of the directory (", chipType, ") must be the same as the chip type
used for the CEL f
at method(static, ...)
at AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("rawData/Monti/HG-U133A")

Other errors appear when I set checkChipType=FALSE:

Error en list(`AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("rawData/Monti/HG-U133A",
checkChipType = FALSE)` = <environment>, :

[2009-08-07 15:15:28] Exception: Could not locate a file for this chip
type: DLBCLwMLBCL.chipA
at throw(Exception(...))
at throw.default("Could not locate a file for this chip type: ",
paste(c(chipType, tags), collapse = ","))
at throw("Could not locate a file for this chip type: ", paste(c
(chipType, tags), collapse = ","))
at method(static, ...)
at AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, nbrOfCells = nbrOfCells)
at method(static, ...)
at AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles("rawData/Monti/HG-U133A",
checkChipType = FALSE)

Everything works fine if the folder I link to has the same name as the
link (e.g. HG-U133A)

So, is there any way to use a soft link to a directory that has not
the same name as the link ?

Thanks in advance,
Hilmar

AFAIK, unfortunately not. Windows Shortcut links are *followed and
expanded* - very much as you do it when you click in the Windows
Explorer - but it is *not remembered what the original link is
located/named. Thus, Windows Shortcuts links are not file links in
the Unix sense.

The parsing of Windows Shortcut files are done by the R.utils package.
You can try this:

1) Create a directory foo/ in the current directory
2) Create a Windows shortcut bar/ linking to foo/
3) In R, do:

library("R.utils");
pathA <- Arguments$getReadablePath("foo");
pathB <- Arguments$getReadablePath("bar");
print(pathA);
[1] "foo"
print(pathB);
[1] "C:/Users/hb/braju.com.R/R.utils,R-forge/foo"
print(identical(getAbsolutePath(pathA), getAbsolutePath(pathB)));
[1] TRUE

As you see, after parsing/expanding bar/, we can no longer tell the
difference between pathA and pathB. This is also how aroma.affymetrix
sees it.

[2 days later and some more thinking]

However, it turns out that your report also points to a "bug"
(actually a feature I though was implemented). In the next release of
aroma.affymetrix, you will be able to do:

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("HG-U133A");
csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("Monti", cdf=cdf);
setFullName(csR, "Monti");

with

<workingDir>/rawData/Monti/HG-U133A[.lnk]/

pointing to

<otherPath>/<otherFullName>/DLBCLwMLBCL.chipA/

To get access to this already now, you can install the "devel" version
(no promises) as:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R");
hbLite(c("R.filesets", "aroma.core"));
installPackages("http://www.braju.com/R/repos/aroma.affymetrix_1.1.3.zip");

Does this work in your case?
